title: Logistic growth: bending to the carrying capacity
subject: math

scenes.caption: The logistic curve bends to the ceiling
scenes.narration: The population grows almost exponentially at first, but as it nears the carrying capacity K the growth slows, the curve bends over and levels exactly at P = K.

shape.explain: Population axis: higher up means a larger population P.
Time axis: further right means later time t.
Carrying-capacity line: the dashed line P = K is the ceiling the population can never pass.
Label: the dashed ceiling is the carrying capacity K.
Label: the vertical axis measures population P.
Label: the horizontal axis measures time t.
Logistic curve: watch it grow in stages - steep at first, then bending over as it nears the ceiling.
Population marker: follow it along the curve as time passes.

steps.text: Growth bends over and levels at P = K: the carrying capacity is the stable equilibrium.

scenes.caption: A slope field funnels all starts to K
scenes.narration: The slope ticks are steep for small populations and flatten near K. Low, middle and high starting curves are all funnelled to the same carrying-capacity equilibrium.

scenes.caption: The equation behind the bend
scenes.narration: The logistic equation dP/dt = rP(1 - P/K) makes the growth rate rise, peak halfway to K, then fall to zero at P = K, which is why the curve levels there.

shape.explain: The logistic equation: the growth rate is rP scaled down by the factor (1 - P/K).
The solution: P(t) starts near zero and rises to level at K as t grows.
Growth-rate axis: higher up means faster growth dP/dt.
Population axis for the growth-rate curve: further right means larger P, with K at the right-hand end.
Label: the vertical axis measures the growth rate.
Label: the horizontal axis measures population P.
Growth-rate curve: it rises to a peak halfway to K, then falls back to zero exactly at P = K.
Label: growth is fastest when the population is halfway to K.
Growth-rate marker: follow it as P grows - the rate climbs, peaks, then dies away to zero at K.
Label: at P = K the growth rate is zero, so the population stops changing.

steps.text: The growth rate itself rises then falls to zero at P = K - that is what bends the population curve level.

scenes.caption: Harvesting drags the equilibrium down
scenes.narration: Harvesting removes population at a steady rate, so the old ceiling no longer balances. The equilibrium line drops to a lower K prime and the population re-settles at the lower ceiling.

shape.explain: Population axis: higher up means a larger population P.
Time axis: further right means later time t.
Old carrying-capacity line: without harvesting the population levels at the original K.
Label: the original carrying capacity, before harvesting.
Settled population: watch its flat tail drop and re-settle once harvesting drags the equilibrium down.
Harvest arrow: steady harvesting pulls the equilibrium down from the old K.
Label: steady harvesting removes population every season.
New equilibrium line: watch it slide down to the lower harvested equilibrium.
Label: the harvested equilibrium sits well below the old K.
Settled-population marker: it ends parked on the lower harvested equilibrium.

steps.text: Harvesting drags the equilibrium down: the population re-settles at a lower ceiling.
